Title: Submission - Cathedral of Flesh (master Tzimisce crypt accelerator)

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Name: Cathedral of Flesh
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 1 pool
Clan: Tzimisce
Master: unique location.
When this card is played, move a Tzimisce with superior Vicissitude [VIC] and capacity 8 or more in your uncontrolled region out of play, face down. At the end of your influence phase, add 3 blood from the bank to this card. If that vampire's capacity is reached or exceeded, return him or her to play in his or her owner's ready region with the blood from this card and burn this card. Any vampire may burn 1 blood on this card as a  action.

Art notes: The inside of a Cathedral. The wall, columns, floor are made of stone that looks organic. Veins in the walls have a faint luminescent glow. The place looks abandonned. The only furnitures are some altar and angel stone statues crying with pain.

World of Darkness reference: Vampire: The Masquerade Revised Edition. Though is it said that the Cathedral of Flesh could be the resting place of Tzimisce himself, it could be in fact the creation of any powerful member of the clan.
Game references: Eternals of Sirius, Gang Territory, tomb of Ramses III

How does this card address a compelling game need? This cards creates a new option to influence out large Tzimisce vampires and is a flavorful addition to the game (with vampires able to fight against the development of the cathedral).
The cards have a few drawbacks:
- you have to influence another Tzimisce first
- it takes a least 3 turns before you get the vampire
- you can't speed up the influence of the vampire (but it can be slowed down by other Methuselahs)
- if the Cathedral is burned (eg. with Arson), the vampire stays out of play and is lost
- it's unique
Advantages:
- it costs only 1 pool for a 8+ Tzimisce at full capacity
- if its changes controller, you still get the Tzimisce in the end
- you can play more than 1 in a game (if you're lucky and manage to protect the counters)
Created by: Ankha

Prince of Paris, France

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body: Great concept, but it looks too strong as it is. It is a 1 pool master that gives you between 8 and 11 free pool and transfers, and all that other players can do about it is slow it down. I would make it burnable as a  action instead. That would make it on par with Powerbase: Baranquilla with respect to raw pool gain but faster. It also gives free transfers but you risk the vampire under it. That sounds about right a clan card. With the Tzimisce disciplines, they have a decent chance to defend it.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
I love it, mostly because it fit with what flesh cathedrales appear to do and mesh with the Tzimisce block thematic.

Like Reyda, I would say burn either all, or at least 3, blood per action, to avoid this becoming out of control. There is a strong element of "the more you win, the more you win", since the more vampire you have, the slimest the chance of stopping the cathedral is.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
The first version of it had only 2 counters per turn, and even with 3 counters per turn, I find it possibly slow. Sure, you get a vampire for 1 pool but you have to wait at least 3 turns to have it (with a setup requiring a least 1 turn), which can be 1/4 of the game. Still, I find Reyda's idea interesting (à la Shatter the Gates), so it could be: "Any vampire may burn the Edge to burn 3 blood on this card as a  action.". It requires only 2 actions (bleeding to get the edge, then removing 3 counters) instead of 3 to get the same result, but requires 1 less block to avoid it.

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
Well, I'd say no, but with one of the deck design questions already being "how do I oust a prey that gains a lot of pool?" I don't think we need this either.

I mean, Tend the Flock creates 3 pool out of nowhere in exchange for an MPA and is considered a pretty damned strong card. Grooming the Protege doesn't create pool, but significantly speeds up the rate at which you can flip vampires and while it's not the best card ever, it sees a fair amount of play. Zillah's Valley costs a pool and only gives you 4 extra transfers for the turn and is played a LOT.

This card changes 1 pool into anywhere between 8 and 11 pool for one MPA and a few turns AND gives a free extra 3 transfers per turn for as long as it takes to bring out whomever you were bringing out.

Yes, it's mostly redundant if you draw it in turn 5+, but so is Zillah's. If you get it early, which isn't exactly a hard feat as shown by everyone drawing their turn-1 Zillah's just fine, it's broken. Flip Horatio turn 1, play CoF turn 2, influence out Meshenka the normal way and get Velya for free by turn 4!

In which universe is this balanced?

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
I think we should distinguish 2 things:
1/ how much the card speeds up the influence of a vampire
2/ hom much blood / pool does the card make the player gain

Concerning 1/ the card is worse than many crypt acceleration if you plan to get that vampire out quickly. With 1 Zillah's Valley, you'd get a vampire in 1 or 2 turns, with Information Highway only 2 turns, even Powerbase: Montreal makes a 10-cap vampire appear in 2 turns.
Cathedral of Flesh requires at least 3 turns, possibly more if people on the table have some actions to spare. Of course, you can influence out other vampires at the same time so it's much like having +3 transfer on the same vampire each turn, which can be slowed down but cost nothing.

Concerning 2/ the card allows you to have a 8+ cap with 8+ blood for 1 pool. It's much better than the aforementioned cards that cost as much pool (+1 for Zillah) as you have blood on the vampire in the end. Some cards already exist that provide free transfer and blood gain (Great Symptosium, Eternals of Sirius), but maybe not as much.

To avoid free transfer + 8+ blood gain, we could consider nerfing the card:

If that vampire's capacity is reached or exceeded, return him or her to play in his or her owner's ready region with 4 blood from this card and burn this card.

(or 3 blood).

One last thing: the card is a location so is vulnerable to many cards.

Messages.Author: Ankha

Here's the previous versions (ideas) of the card:

Name: Cathedral of Flesh
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 1 pool
Clan: Tzimisce
Master: unique location.
When this card is played, move a Tzimisce with superior Vicissitude [VIC] and capacity 8 or more in your uncontrolled region out of play, face down. At the end of your influence phase, discard a retainer or ally from your hand to add 3 blood from the bank to this card. If that vampire's capacity is reached or exceeded, return him or her to play in his or her owner's ready region with the blood from this card and burn this card.

This version is more proactive than passive.

Another idea:
Name: Cathedral of Flesh
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 1 pool
Clan: Tzimisce
Master: unique location.
When this card is played, move a Tzimisce with superior Vicissitude [VIC] and capacity 8 or more in your uncontrolled region out of play, face down, and remove a ready Tzimisce you control with capacity X from the game. At the end of your influence phase, add X blood from the bank to this card. If that vampire's capacity is reached or exceeded, return him or her to play in his or her owner's ready region with the blood from this card and burn this card.
